name: Late-onset Primary Lymphedema Without Systemic or Visceral Involvement

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical Diagnostic Criteria for Late-onset Primary Lymphedema

criteria.description: Chronic, progressive unilateral or bilateral swelling of the lower limbs without systemic cause
Exclusion of secondary causes such as infection, malignancy, trauma, or venous insufficiency
Imaging evidence of lymphatic dysfunction on lymphoscintigraphy or equivalent modality
Symptom onset typically after puberty or in early adulthood
No evidence of systemic or visceral organ involvement

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of all major criteria including chronic limb swelling, exclusion of secondary causes, and confirmatory lymphatic imaging
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is clinical supported by imaging; genetic testing may be considered but is not mandatory.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Non-pitting edema of the lower extremities
pathognomonic.notes: Typically affects feet and distal legs

pathognomonic.symptomName: Stemmer sign positivity (inability to pinch skin at base of second toe)
searchTerms: unable to pinch skin on toe

pathognomonic.symptomName: Progressive limb volume increase without systemic symptoms
pathognomonic.notes: Chronic progression over months to years
searchTerms: gradual limb swelling without other symptoms
limb volume increase without systemic signs

common.symptomName: Skin thickening and fibrosis over affected limb
searchTerms: skin thickening and hardening over limb
fibrotic skin changes on affected limb

common.symptomName: Heaviness or discomfort in affected limb
searchTerms: heaviness or aching in affected limb
frequent episodes of skin redness and swelling

common.symptomName: Positive Stemmer sign on affected limb
searchTerms: unable to pinch skin fold on limb
thickened rough skin with wart-like bumps
skin with excess keratin and papillomas

occasional.symptomName: Limited joint mobility due to swelling
searchTerms: limited joint movement due to swelling

occasional.notes: Usually related to swelling and tissue changes
searchTerms: mild aching or pain in limbs

occasional.notes: May coexist but not primary cause
searchTerms: signs of poor vein function like varicose veins

rare.symptomName: Systemic symptoms such as fever or malaise

laboratory: Elevated inflammatory markers during cellulitis episodes
imaging: Lymphoscintigraphy showing delayed or absent lymphatic drainage
Ultrasound excluding venous thrombosis or insufficiency
genetic: Possible mutations in FLT4 (VEGFR3) gene in some familial cases
other: Absence of systemic or visceral organ abnormalities

distinguishingFeatures: History of surgery, trauma, infection, or malignancy
Presence of systemic or visceral involvement
Imaging showing obstruction or damage to lymphatics secondary to external cause
Presence of varicose veins and venous stasis changes

redFlags: Presence of systemic symptoms such as fever or weight loss
Signs of malignancy or lymphangiosarcoma development
references: Orphanet: Late-onset Primary Lymphedema Without Systemic or Visceral Involvement, ORPHA:289825
Rockson SG. Lymphedema. Am J Med. 2001;110(4):288-295.
